studies.Timing: Diet assessed at baseline with average follow-up of nine years
studies.comparison_type: Highest vs lowest quintile of dietary eicosapentaenoic acid intake (Q5 vs Q1)
studies.exposure_measurement_supporting_text: Diet was assessed at baseline with self-administered food-frequency questionnaires.

cases.excerpt: Among 288,268 men with average follow-up of nine years, 23,281 prostate cancer cases (18,934 nonadvanced and 2,930 advanced including 725 fatal cases) were identified.

comparison.excerpt: HRQ5 vs. Q1, 0.82

continent.excerpt: NIH-American Association of Retired Persons (AARP) Diet and Health Study

design.excerpt: HR and 95% confidence intervals (CI) were estimated with Cox proportional hazards models.

effect_size.excerpt: Eicosapentanoic acid (EPA) intake was related to decreased risk of fatal prostate cancer (HRQ5 vs. Q1, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.64-1.04; Ptrend = 0.02).
